method.method_draft: Let M(f) be zero outside |f|≤100 Hz. Use the Hilbert-transform spectrum \hat M(f)=−jsgn(f)M(f). Write the Fourier transform of s(t)=m(t)cos(2πf_ct)−\hat m(t)sin(2πf_ct) as shifted copies of M(f) and \hat M(f). Combining the cos and sin terms cancels one sideband and retains only a single translated band, e.g. from fc to fc+100 Hz or from fc−100 Hz to fc depending on sign convention. The width of that remaining occupied band is 100 Hz, so the bandwidth of s(t) is 100 Hz.

Let M(f) be the spectrum of m(t). Since m(t) has bandwidth 100 Hz, M(f)=0 outside |f|≤100 Hz. The Hilbert transform spectrum is M_hat(f) = -j sgn(f) M(f). For s(t)=m(t)cos(2πf_c t)-m_hat(t)sin(2πf_c t), the Fourier transform consists of shifted copies of M(f) and M_hat(f). Around +f_c, set ν=f-f_c. The spectrum there is proportional to M(ν)+jM_hat(ν)=M(ν)+j[-j sgn(ν)M(ν)]=[1+sgn(ν)]M(ν). Thus the negative-frequency baseband portion cancels and only one sideband remains. With f_c=1000 Hz and baseband bandwidth 100 Hz, the retained positive-frequency band is from 1000 Hz to 1100 Hz, whose width is 100 Hz. Equivalently, depending on sideband sign convention, a single sideband of width 100 Hz is retained.
